lines: Revisiting his talk with NextEra CEO John Ketchum, Nicolai Tangen says AI data centers have turned power from a stagnant sector into a high-growth one, with NextEra projecting US demand to rise sixfold by the mid-2040s and the industry spending upwards of $1 billion a week on build-out.

Because hyperscalers need 24/7 base load that intermittent renewables can't supply, the episode says nuclear and large-scale battery storage are becoming critical, and established tech giants gain an edge by locking in long-term power early.

NBIM is leaning into the shift by expanding its unlisted renewables portfolio, including a recent 10% stake in a major US battery platform; Tangen argues entry points improved after the earlier green-energy froth cooled.

Headwinds include local opposition to data centers over rising electricity bills and AI-driven job fears, while business leaders he met flag a 'Dark October' surge in cyberattacks alongside persistent inflation risk.
podcast: In Good Company with Nicolai Tangen
title: Friday Wrap-Up: Nuclear, Batteries and Reflections from New York
